observations.observation: Bloomberg’s first report said Oracle sent a force-majeure notice to the Project Jupiter developer and, according to people familiar, sought payment relief if the campus missed its planned 2028 start rather than exiting as tenant. The notice’s exact delivery time was not reported.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This was anonymous-source reporting, not a public copy of the notice. Bloomberg said it was uncertain the notice would release Oracle from existing obligations; it did not report a confirmed cancellation or revised project date.

observations.observation: The supplied Reuters roundup linked the notice to possible delays securing power, based on a person familiar with the matter. This is a cause-specific report, not a disclosed project milestone or a published contract trigger.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The provided source metadata is date-level. The report identifies no specific permit, fuel, interconnection gate, revised commissioning date, or scope reduction.

observations.observation: By the cutoff, Oracle publicly maintained that Project Jupiter remained on schedule; Blue Owl said the notice did not change the project’s financial commitments and that the parties remained aligned.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These are company statements, not independent evidence that power, permits, or project milestones were secured; they do not disclose the notice’s terms.

observations.observation: Before the notice, Oracle, BorderPlex, and Bloom had announced a planned Bloom fuel-cell design for up to 2.45 GW, replacing the earlier gas-turbine and diesel design. Oracle’s September 14 statement separately said the data-center buildings and proposed microgrid had distinct permitting status.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The 2.45 GW was an announced maximum design, not evidence of installed or accepted Bloom capacity. Oracle’s September 14 permitting statement preceded the September 17 court order.

observations.observation: The New Mexico Supreme Court’s September 17 order denied petitions and lifted stays, but did not issue the microgrid air permit. Separately, FERC’s September 10 notice described the proposed Green Chile gas pipeline’s environmental assessment as open for comment and not a decision document.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: FERC staff’s environmental conclusion was potentially supportive but did not amount to final authorization; neither record establishes a project-specific power shortfall or delay.

observations.observation: The supplied Reuters roundup also described a global bond selloff, elevated yields, and weak Treasury-auction demand as concurrent macro topics, separate from its Project Jupiter report.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The roundup does not connect these macro items to Project Jupiter or Bloom. Market-close reactions and prices are not used.

gaps: No publicly accessible copy of Oracle’s force-majeure notice or the relevant lease/power contract was located; its precise legal trigger, terms, acceptance, and notice-delivery time remain unverified.
No pre-cutoff source establishes a missed project milestone, cancellation, revised Bloom scope, installed/accepted Bloom capacity, or project-specific firm power availability.
The FERC environmental assessment is not an authorization decision; the reviewed record does not establish final pipeline authorization or completed fuel delivery.
The supplied Reuters source uses date-level publication-time metadata. Its captured text predates cutoff, but its wider market-close and price commentary was excluded.
research_notes: Cutoff: 2026-09-24T21:09:10.560684Z. The earliest traceable report found was Bloomberg at 08:25 EDT (12:25Z), citing people familiar with the matter. Counterevidence available by cutoff: Oracle said the project remained on schedule and Blue Owl said the notice did not change its financial commitments.
